text_mt: When the concluding purificatory offering is completed, having touched the water with 'O concluding purificatory bath, Nicumpuṇa! Thou art Niceru, O Nicumpuṇa! May I have wiped away by the gods the sin done against the gods, and by mortals that done against mortals; protect me, O god, from harm caused by the deceitful' (avabhṛtha nicuṃpuṇa...), they should sprinkle themselves three times.

sanskrit_iast: ādityamupatiṣṭherannudvayantamasaspari jyotiḥ paśyanta uttaraṃ svaḥ paśyanta uttaraṃ devaṃ devatrā sūryyamaganma jyotiruttamamiti
meaning: आदित्यमुपतिष्ठेरन्नुद्वयन्तमसस्परि ज्योतिः पश्यन्त उत्तरं स्वः पश्यन्त उत्तरं देवं देवत्रा सूर्य्यमगन्म ज्योतिरुत्तममिति
text_mt: They should attend upon the sun with: 'Arising from darkness, beholding the higher light, beholding the higher heaven, the god among the gods, we have attained the sun, the supreme light' (ud vayaṃ tamasas pari...).
If it has set, [they attend upon] the āhavanīya fire.

sanskrit_iast: tasmin samidha ādadhyuredhosyedhiṣīmahīti prathamā samidasi samedhiṣīmahīti dvitīyāṃ yadenaścakṛmā vayaṃ yadvānyakṛtamārimānayā samidhā vay sarvantadapamṛjya ha iti tṛtīyām
meaning: तस्मिन् समिध आदध्युरेधोस्येधिषीमहीति प्रथमा समिदसि समेधिषीमहीति द्वितीयां यदेनश्चकृमा वयं यद्वान्यकृतमारिमानया समिधा वय् सर्वन्तदपमृज्य ह इति तृतीयाम्
text_mt: They should put kindling sticks on it: the first with 'Thou art kindling, may we thrive' (edho 'sy edhiṣīmahi); the second with 'Thou art kindling, may we prosper' (samid asi samedhiṣīmahi); the third with 'Whatever sin we have committed, or what committed by another we have encountered, with this kindling stick may we wipe it all away' (yad enaś cakṛmā vayam...).

sanskrit_iast: tamevopatiṣṭherannapo adyānvacāriṣaṃ rasena samaganmahi payasvānagna āgamantaṃ mā ssṛja varcaseti
meaning: तमेवोपतिष्ठेरन्नपो अद्यान्वचारिषं रसेन समगन्महि पयस्वानग्न आगमन्तं मा स्सृज वर्चसेति
text_mt: They should attend upon that very fire with: 'We have entered the waters today, we have united with their essence; having come, rich in sap, O Agni, unite me with brilliance' (apo adyānvacāriṣam...).
Before the concluding atirātra sacrifice, the day ends with the apsuṣoma rites in sacrificial sessions.
In multi-day sacrifices, it ends with the consumption of curd.

sanskrit_iast: yāvantyahāni rājānaṃ bhakṣayeyustāvatsvabrāhmaṇāyocchiṣṭaṃ na dadyuradbhirvā prokṣya dadyuḥ
meaning: यावन्त्यहानि राजानं भक्षयेयुस्तावत्स्वब्राह्मणायोच्छिष्टं न दद्युरद्भिर्वा प्रोक्ष्य दद्युः
text_mt: As many days as they consume King [Soma], for so long they should not give the leftover food to a brāhmaṇa of their own, or they may give it having sprinkled it with water.

sanskrit_iast: tadeṣa ślokaḥ somametat pivata yat kiñcāśnīta brāhmaṇā mābrāhmaṇāyocchiṣṭaṃ dāta mā pātsomamasomapa iti
meaning: तदेष श्लोकः सोममेतत् पिवत यत् किञ्चाश्नीत ब्राह्मणा माब्राह्मणायोच्छिष्टं दात मा पात्सोममसोमप इति

text_mt: One should know this rule of conduct in all sacrifices, in all sacrifices.

sanskrit_iast: ṣoḍaśisāmnā stoṣyamāṇo yathāsanamupaviśya havirddhānaṃ gatvā ṣoḍaśigrahamavekṣetodgātā yasmādanya iti
meaning: षोडशिसाम्ना स्तोष्यमाणो यथासनमुपविश्य हविर्द्धानं गत्वा षोडशिग्रहमवेक्षेतोद्गाता यस्मादन्य इति
title: tṛtīyaḥ prapāṭhakaḥ — atha prathamā kaṇḍikā
text_mt: When about to chant with the ṣoḍaśin melody, having sat in his proper seat and gone to the havirdhāna shed, the udgātṛ priest should look upon the ṣoḍaśin cup with: 'Other than whom...'.
and also if they draw [it] at the subsequent two [pressings].

sanskrit_iast: aśvaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ pūrvasyāṃ sadaso dvāri pratyaṅmakhastiṣṭhediti dhānañjayyaḥ
meaning: अश्वः कृष्णः पूर्वस्यां सदसो द्वारि प्रत्यङ्मखस्तिष्ठेदिति धानञ्जय्यः
text_mt: A black horse should stand at the eastern door of the sadas, facing west—thus says Dhānañjayya.
At the western [door], facing east—thus says Śāṇḍilya.
In the absence of that, whatever horse [is available].
The udgātṛ priest [should do so] as they join in the cadence.
When [the sun] sinks, he should sing the first round softly.
When it has set, the second with a middle tone.
Whenever they bring [it] on, they should chant immediately.
By day softly; at night aloud.
In sacrifices with fees, one should give the horse and the gold to the udgātṛ priest.

sanskrit_iast: satra eva grahasya bhakṣayeyuraindrsaha ityudasya harivadaharikāsu cet stuvīran
meaning: सत्र एव ग्रहस्य भक्षयेयुरैन्द्र्सह इत्युदस्य हरिवदहरिकासु चेत् स्तुवीरन्
text_mt: Only at a sacrificial session should they consume the cup with: 'Indra's power...', having set aside [the formula with] the bays, if they chant on verses containing the word 'hari'.
[They consume the portion] of the goblet with the anuṣṭubh metre,

sanskrit_iast: tathā kurvannindraśca samrāḍvaruṇasya rājā tau te bhakṣyaṃ cakraturagra etaṃ tayorahamanubhakṣyaṃ bhakṣayāmi vāgjuṣāṇā somasya tṛpyatviti grahasya
meaning: तथा कुर्वन्निन्द्रश्च सम्राड्वरुणस्य राजा तौ ते भक्ष्यं चक्रतुरग्र एतं तयोरहमनुभक्ष्यं भक्षयामि वाग्जुषाणा सोमस्य तृप्यत्विति ग्रहस्य
text_mt: Doing so, [he consumes] the cup with: 'Both Indra the sovereign and king Varuṇa, they made this portion for you in the beginning; I consume their after-portion; may Speech, taking pleasure in Soma, be satisfied!'
Or with: 'Indra indeed...', adding the formula: 'May the goddess Speech drink of the Soma!'

sanskrit_iast: aindr saha iti camasasyāsatre triṣṭupchandasā vājapeyasāmni bhakṣayediti gautamaḥ
meaning: ऐन्द्र् सह इति चमसस्यासत्रे त्रिष्टुप्छन्दसा वाजपेयसाम्नि भक्षयेदिति गौतमः
text_mt: Outside a sacrificial session, one should consume [the portion] of the goblet with: 'Indra's power...', using the triṣṭubh metre at the vājapeya melody—thus says Gautama.
With the anuṣṭubh metre—thus say Dhānañjayya and Śāṇḍilya.
With the anuṣṭubh metre at night.
At the twilight laud, they should utter 'hiṃ' separately for the triplets.
The consumption takes place with: 'Of the offering-yajus...'.
With the gāyatrī metre in the extra stotras—thus says Gautama.
In succession with the different metres belonging to the consumption—thus say Dhānañjayya and Śāṇḍilya.

title: atha dvitīyā kaṇḍikā
text_mt: One who has established the sacred fires but not performed a soma sacrifice, having performed a soma sacrifice through another, should perform the substitute consumption.
Even one who has performed a soma sacrifice—thus says Śāṇḍilya.
When the morning offering has been offered, having placed ghee on the gārhapatya fire, he should remove it towards the north.
Having placed drops [of curd] into a bowl or a goblet, he should deposit it near the dakṣiṇāgni fire,

sanskrit_iast: paścimena gārhapatyaṃ gatvā paścādāhavanīyasyopaviśya sruveṇa srucyājyaṃ gṛhṇīyādyāvadgṛhītī syāt
meaning: पश्चिमेन गार्हपत्यं गत्वा पश्चादाहवनीयस्योपविश्य स्रुवेण स्रुच्याज्यं गृह्णीयाद्यावद्गृहीती स्यात्
text_mt: Having gone around to the west of the gārhapatya fire and sat behind the āhavanīya fire, he should take ghee into the offering ladle with the dipping spoon, as much as should be taken.

sanskrit_iast: tajjuhuyādimāmagne śaraṇiṃ mīmṛṣo na imamadhvānaṃ yamagāma dūramāpiḥ pitā pramatiḥ somyānāṃ bhrimiraspṛṣi kṛnmartyānāsvāheti
meaning: तज्जुहुयादिमामग्ने शरणिं मीमृषो न इममध्वानं यमगाम दूरमापिः पिता प्रमतिः सोम्यानां भ्रिमिरस्पृषि कृन्मर्त्यानास्वाहेति
text_mt: He should offer it with: 'O Agni, forgive this our wandering, this far path that we have traveled; you are a friend, father, protector of the soma-offerers, an agitator, touching mortals; svāhā!'

sanskrit_iast: evameva gṛhītvāpāṃ puṣpamastyoṣadhīnā rasogneḥ priyatamā tanūrindrasya priyatamhaviḥ svāheti
meaning: एवमेव गृहीत्वापां पुष्पमस्त्योषधीना रसोग्नेः प्रियतमा तनूरिन्द्रस्य प्रियतम्हविः स्वाहेति
text_mt: Having taken [ghee] in the very same way, [he offers with]: 'You are the flower of the waters, the sap of plants, the dearest body of Agni, the dearest oblation of Indra; svāhā!'

sanskrit_iast: ājyasya pūrvān grahān gṛhītvā dadhna uttamaṃ viśvebhyo devebhyaḥ svāheti
meaning: आज्यस्य पूर्वान् ग्रहान् गृहीत्वा दध्न उत्तमं विश्वेभ्यो देवेभ्यः स्वाहेति
text_mt: Having drawn the earlier draughts of ghee, [he offers] the final [draught] of curd with: 'To all the gods, svāhā!'

sanskrit_iast: dadhiśeṣsrucyānīyodaṅṅāvṛtya prāśnīyāttava soma vrate vayaṃ manastanūṣu piprataḥ prajāvanto aśīmahīti
meaning: दधिशेष्स्रुच्यानीयोदङ्ङावृत्य प्राश्नीयात्तव सोम व्रते वयं मनस्तनूषु पिप्रतः प्रजावन्तो अशीमहीति
text_mt: Having poured the remainder of the curd into the offering ladle and turned towards the north, he should eat it with: 'In your service, O Soma, filling our mind in our bodies, may we, possessing offspring, enjoy [you]!'

sanskrit_iast: prakṣālya srucaṃ yathetaṃ pratyāvrajya prācīnāvītī bhūtvā dakṣiṇā dakṣiṇāgneḥ sthaṇḍil samuhyādbhiḥ samprokṣya sphyena sakṛdullikhyolmukamupanidhāya darbhānupastīryāpa upaninīyāmīṣāṃ drapsānānnipṛṇuyādavamebhyaḥ pitṛbhyaḥ svadhā saha bhakṣebhya iti prathamam
meaning: प्रक्षाल्य स्रुचं यथेतं प्रत्याव्रज्य प्राचीनावीती भूत्वा दक्षिणा दक्षिणाग्नेः स्थण्डिल् समुह्याद्भिः सम्प्रोक्ष्य स्फ्येन सकृदुल्लिख्योल्मुकमुपनिधाय दर्भानुपस्तीर्याप उपनिनीयामीषां द्रप्सानान्निपृणुयादवमेभ्यः पितृभ्यः स्वधा सह भक्षेभ्य इति प्रथमम्
text_mt: Having washed the offering ladle, returned the way he came, and worn the sacred cord over the right shoulder, having swept a raised mound to the south of the dakṣiṇāgni fire, sprinkled it with water, furrowed it once with the wooden sword, placed a firebrand beside it, spread darbha grass, and poured out water, he should offer the first of these drops with: 'To the lowest fathers, svadhā, together with the portions!'
With: 'To the Aurvas, to the Kāvyas', in the very same manner to the south, separately.

sanskrit_iast: atra pitaro mādayadhvaṃ yathābhāgamityuktvodaṅṅāvarttetāsitvā yāvanmanyeta tāvadabhiparyāvarttamāno japedamīmadanta pitaro yathābhāgamanantaritāḥ pitaraḥ somapīthāditi
meaning: अत्र पितरो मादयध्वं यथाभागमित्युक्त्वोदङ्ङावर्त्तेतासित्वा यावन्मन्येत तावदभिपर्यावर्त्तमानो जपेदमीमदन्त पितरो यथाभागमनन्तरिताः पितरः सोमपीथादिति
text_mt: Having said: 'Here, O fathers, rejoice each according to his share!', he should turn towards the north; having sat for as long as he thinks fit, turning towards [them], he should mutter: 'The fathers have rejoiced, each according to his share, not excluded from the soma-drink.'
He should cast that darbha grass and the drops into the dakṣiṇāgni fire.

sanskrit_iast: yajñopavītī bhūtvāpa upaspṛśya gṛhān vrajañjapedgṛhā mā bibhīta mā vepiḍhvamūrjaṃ bibhrata evamasyūrjaṃ bibhradvaḥ sumanāḥ sumedhā gṛhānemi manasā daivena yeṣāmadhyeti pravasanneṣu saumanaso bahurgṛhānupahūyāmahe te no jānantu jānataḥ upahūtā iha gāva upahūtā ajāvayo'tho annasya yo rasa upahūto gṛheṣu na iti
meaning: यज्ञोपवीती भूत्वाप उपस्पृश्य गृहान् व्रजञ्जपेद्गृहा मा बिभीत मा वेपिढ्वमूर्जं बिभ्रत एवमस्यूर्जं बिभ्रद्वः सुमनाः सुमेधा गृहानेमि मनसा दैवेन येषामध्येति प्रवसन्नेषु सौमनसो बहुर्गृहानुपहूयामहे ते नो जानन्तु जानतः उपहूता इह गाव उपहूता अजावयोऽथो अन्नस्य यो रस उपहूतो गृहेषु न इति
title: atha tṛtīyā kaṇḍikā
text_mt: Having worn the sacred cord over the left shoulder and touched water, going toward his house he should mutter: 'O house, do not fear, do not tremble, bearing nourishment... Bearing your nourishment, well-minded, wise, I come to the house with divine intent; whoever thinks of them while away, great friendliness is in them. We invoke the house; may they, knowing, know us! Invoked here are cows, invoked goats and sheep, and whatever sap of food [there is], is invoked in our house!'

sanskrit_iast: paścācchālāgnerupaviśya japediha gāvaḥ prajāyadhvamihāśvā iha puruṣā iho sahasradakṣiṇo'pi pūṣā niṣīdatviti
meaning: पश्चाच्छालाग्नेरुपविश्य जपेदिह गावः प्रजायध्वमिहाश्वा इह पुरुषा इहो सहस्रदक्षिणोऽपि पूषा निषीदत्विति
text_mt: Sitting behind the hall-fire, he should mutter: 'Here, cows, propagate; here horses, here men; and here may Pūṣan of a thousand gifts also sit down!'
Having pushed back the grasses of the fire, he should converse with whomever is his friend.

sanskrit_iast: goṣu gā apisṛjedupedamupaparcanamāsu goṣūpapṛcyatāmuparṣabhasya retasyupendra tava vīryya iti
meaning: गोषु गा अपिसृजेदुपेदमुपपर्चनमासु गोषूपपृच्यतामुपर्षभस्य रेतस्युपेन्द्र तव वीर्य्य इति
text_mt: He should let loose cows among the cows with: 'Towards this uniting, let it unite with these cows; towards the semen of the bull; towards your power, O Indra!'
In sacrificial sessions, the adhvaryu priest should consecrate everyone.

sanskrit_iast: dīkṣiṣyamāṇāndarśayet svastyātreyamarundhatīṃ dhruvamudapātraṃ ya eṣo'kṣiṇi puruṣo dṛśyate
meaning: दीक्षिष्यमाणान्दर्शयेत् स्वस्त्यात्रेयमरुन्धतीं ध्रुवमुदपात्रं य एषोऽक्षिणि पुरुषो दृश्यते
text_mt: To those about to be consecrated, he should show the Svastyātreya [star], Arundhatī, the pole star, a water-vessel, and this person who is seen in the eye.
[If] one whose life has departed does not see these,

sanskrit_iast: dīkṣiṣyamāṇāḥ saṃvaderan saha naḥ sādhukṛtyā nānā pāpakṛtyā yāsminsatre
meaning: दीक्षिष्यमाणाः संवदेरन् सह नः साधुकृत्या नाना पापकृत्या यास्मिन्सत्रे
text_mt: Those about to be consecrated should make a mutual declaration: 'Together is our good deed, separate our bad deed, in this sacrificial session.'

sanskrit_iast: atha yatpurā cakṛma karttāsmaśca yathopasthitameva nastaditi
meaning: अथ यत्पुरा चकृम कर्त्तास्मश्च यथोपस्थितमेव नस्तदिति
text_mt: "Now, whatever we have done previously, or are going to do, that belongs to us just as it has occurred."
Beginning from their consecration, their eating and sleeping should take place in the wife's hall (patnīśālā).
Beginning from the fast-day (upavasathya), [they should take place] in the āgnīdhra shed (āgnīdrīya).
At the times of twilight, they should restrain their speech.
They should speak speech ending with the word 'vicakṣaṇa' ('discerning').
They should not salute anyone.
They should not converse with a Śūdra.
They should not go out through the western door of the wife's hall.
They should void their excrement facing east or north.
No one else should look at them from this [time onwards].
They should partake of [the remnants of] all the soma-pressing sessions.
They should avoid anger and falsehood.
When they have glided out beyond the vedi, they should avoid sunrise and sunset, and making the call.

title: atha caturthī kaṇḍikā
text_mt: If any fault should befall any of these three, they should seek ritual invitation from the householder (gṛhapati).
Or from all of them according to the order of consecration.
When the vasatīvarī waters have been carried around, they should lie down to rest.
If any of them should die, carrying him out by the untrodden path (atīrtha), they should cremate him with the kitchen fire (āhārya) if he has not established the sacred fires.

Having caused the fires to ascend into the two kindling sticks, and carrying these two out through the passage (āpnāna), [they should cremate him] with churned fire if he has established the sacred fires.

sanskrit_iast: madhyamasya rātriparyyāyasya daivodāsaṃ hotṛṣāma syādaurddhasadmanaṃ vā
meaning: मध्यमस्य रात्रिपर्य्यायस्य दैवोदासं होतृषाम स्यादौर्द्धसद्मनं वा
text_mt: The Daivodāsa sāman should be the hotṛ-sāman of the middle night round (rātriparyāya), or the Aurddhasadmana.

sanskrit_iast: abhiplavasya dvitīye'hani bhargo yaśa iti prāgviṣuvato vyatyāsaṃ syātāmiti gautamaḥ
meaning: अभिप्लवस्य द्वितीयेऽहनि भर्गो यश इति प्राग्विषुवतो व्यत्यासं स्यातामिति गौतमः
text_mt: On the second day of the abhiplava six-day period, before the viṣuvat day, Bharga and Yaśas should be alternated: thus says Gautama.
And after [the viṣuvat], in three abhiplavas.
Yaśas should be once or twice before, and likewise Bharga after, and in the others [vice versa]: thus another view.
Bharga should be in the earlier half, Yaśas in the later: thus another view.
By these two, the Vīṅka and Śuddhāśuddhīya [sāmans] are explained.
After the viṣuvat day, there should only be the Vīṅka: thus says Dhānañjayya.
On the fifth day, there should be the unbroken series of village-sung chants, and it should be prior to the Mānava [sāman].
The Iṣovṛdhīya and Samanta should be on the sixth [day] immediately following the pṛṣṭhya six-day period.
In the first half, among the three, the fourth abhiplava should be omitted.
These very abhiplavas are reversed after the viṣuvat day.
They should perform their days in reverse order.

sanskrit_iast: daśarātrasamīpe triṣu caturṇāmāvṛttānāṃ prathamo lupyeteti dhānañjayya uttama iṣovṛdhīyasamante syātāmiti
meaning: दशरात्रसमीपे त्रिषु चतुर्णामावृत्तानां प्रथमो लुप्येतेति धानञ्जय्य उत्तम इषोवृधीयसमन्ते स्यातामिति
text_mt: Near the ten-night period, among the three, the first of the four reversed [abhiplavas] should be omitted: thus says Dhānañjayya; and the Iṣovṛdhīya and Samanta should be at the very end.
The reverse of this is the view of Śāṇḍilyāyana.
In the three, there is absence of the Iṣovṛdhīya and Samanta.
However, the opinion of the teachers is that there is presence; the opinion of the teachers is that there is presence.

sanskrit_iast: pṛṣṭye rathamativaheyuḥ paścāt prāñcaṃ dakṣiṇato vodañcaṃ bahirvedi rathantarasya stotre
meaning: पृष्ट्ये रथमतिवहेयुः पश्चात् प्राञ्चं दक्षिणतो वोदञ्चं बहिर्वेदि रथन्तरस्य स्तोत्रे
title: atha pañcamī kaṇḍikā
text_mt: In the pṛṣṭhya six-day period, outside the vedi, they should drive a chariot across from west to east, or from south to north, at the stotra of the Rathantara.
At [the stotra] of the Bṛhat, they should beat a war drum.
Fanning themselves, or being fanned, they should chant praise with the Vairūpa.

sanskrit_iast: vācayitvā yajamānaṃ stutamasītyanena vāta ā vātviti tṛcenānumantrayet
meaning: वाचयित्वा यजमानं स्तुतमसीत्यनेन वात आ वात्विति तृचेनानुमन्त्रयेत्
text_mt: Having made the patron of the sacrifice recite 'You are praised', he should consecrate with the triplet 'May the wind blow here' (vāta ā vātu).

sanskrit_iast: vairājasya stotra upākṛta uparyyanūrusakalaṃ nidhāya tṛṇe ca tasyopari tiraścīmaraṇiṃ nidhāyābhyātmaṃ prajananaṃ kṛtvā triḥ pradakṣiṇamabhimanthedgāyatraṃ chando'nuprajāyasva traiṣṭubhaṃ jāgatamānuṣṭubhaṃ vairājamiti gautamaḥ
meaning: वैराजस्य स्तोत्र उपाकृत उपर्य्यनूरुसकलं निधाय तृणे च तस्योपरि तिरश्चीमरणिं निधायाभ्यात्मं प्रजननं कृत्वा त्रिः प्रदक्षिणमभिमन्थेद्गायत्रं छन्दोऽनुप्रजायस्व त्रैष्टुभं जागतमानुष्टुभं वैराजमिति गौतमः
text_mt: When the stotra of the Vairāja has been commenced, placing a thigh-high piece of wood above and two blades of grass upon it, placing the kindling stick transversely upon that, and directing the socket towards oneself, he should churn [fire] three times clockwise with: 'Be born in accordance with the gāyatrī meter, traiṣṭubha, jāgata, ānuṣṭubha, and vairāja': thus says Gautama.

sanskrit_iast: araṇyoḥ sandhānamālabhyopajighret tejo'si tejo mayi dhehīti
meaning: अरण्योः सन्धानमालभ्योपजिघ्रेत् तेजोऽसि तेजो मयि धेहीति
text_mt: Touching the joint of the two kindling sticks, he should smell it with: 'You are splendor; bestow splendor in me.'
While it is being churned, he should yoke the stoma.

sanskrit_iast: vācayitvā yajamānaṃ punarūrjā nivarttasva punaragna iṣāyuṣā punarnaḥ pāhyhasaḥ saha rathyā nivarttasvāgne pinvasva dhārayā viśvapsyā viśvatasparītyanumantryābhijuhuyāttaduktaṃ brāhmaṇena
meaning: वाचयित्वा यजमानं पुनरूर्जा निवर्त्तस्व पुनरग्न इषायुषा पुनर्नः पाह्य्हसः सह रथ्या निवर्त्तस्वाग्ने पिन्वस्व धारया विश्वप्स्या विश्वतस्परीत्यनुमन्त्र्याभिजुहुयात्तदुक्तं ब्राह्मणेन
text_mt: Having made the patron of the sacrifice recite, having consecrated with 'Return with sap, O Agni, return with nourishment and life; protect us again from distress; return with wealth, O Agni, overflow with a all-nourishing stream from every side', he should offer an oblation; that is stated by the Brāhmaṇa.
Placing water with avakā plants nearby, they should chant praise with the Mahānāmnī verses.

sanskrit_iast: yo yaḥ sāmāṅge brūyātsa udaghoṣaṃ janayet
meaning: यो यः सामाङ्गे ब्रूयात्स उदघोषं जनयेत्

sanskrit_iast: vācayitvā yajamānaṃ tā ninayedāstāve'nādhṛṣṭāsi tāntvā somo rājā vanuyāma pītā upatiṣṭhanta āpo ye śākkarā ṛṣabhā ye svarājaste arṣantu te varṣantu te kṛṇvantviṣamūrjrāyaspoṣantadbideyeti
meaning: वाचयित्वा यजमानं ता निनयेदास्तावेऽनाधृष्टासि तान्त्वा सोमो राजा वनुयाम पीता उपतिष्ठन्त आपो ये शाक्करा ऋषभा ये स्वराजस्ते अर्षन्तु ते वर्षन्तु ते कृण्वन्त्विषमूर्ज्रायस्पोषन्तद्बिदेयेति
text_mt: Having caused the patron of the sacrifice to recite, he should pour out those [waters] at the āstāva with: 'Unassailable art thou; may we obtain thee whom King Soma has drunk; waters that attend, bulls of the Śakvarī verse, who are self-ruling, let them flow, let them rain, let them bring refreshment, vigor, wealth, and prosperity; so may it be.'
Or with: 'I send you to the ocean...'
They should push the avakā plants up to the knees.
One desiring rain should have him sit on the roof-covering [of the cart-shed], so says Śāṇḍilya.

sanskrit_iast: vāravantīyasya stotre dhenuḥ saṃvāśayeyurdakṣiṇataḥ kṛtvottarato vatsān
meaning: वारवन्तीयस्य स्तोत्रे धेनुः संवाशयेयुर्दक्षिणतः कृत्वोत्तरतो वत्सान्
title: atha ṣaṣṭhī kaṇḍikā
text_mt: During the stotra of the Vāravantīya [sāman], they should cause the milk cows to low, having placed them to the south and the calves to the north.
Having united them to the east of the sadas, they should release them northward behind the āgnīdhra fire.

sanskrit_iast: vācayitvā yajamānaṃ gonāmabhiranumantrayeta havye kāmye candre jyota iḍe rante juṣṭe sṛnari mayi vo rāyaḥ ayantāmiḍa ehyadita ehi juṣṭe juṣṭinte gameyamupahūtā upahavaṃ vośīyeti
meaning: वाचयित्वा यजमानं गोनामभिरनुमन्त्रयेत हव्ये काम्ये चन्द्रे ज्योत इडे रन्ते जुष्टे सृनरि मयि वो रायः अयन्तामिड एह्यदित एहि जुष्टे जुष्टिन्ते गमेयमुपहूता उपहवं वोशीयेति
text_mt: Having caused the patron of the sacrifice to recite, he should address them with the names of the cows: 'O offering, desirable one, shining one, bright one, O Iḍā, delightful one, pleasing one, noble woman, let your wealth abide in me; come, O Iḍā; come, O Aditi; pleasing one, may I enter into your favor; being invited, may I obtain your ritual invitation.'
If they commence [the stotra] with waters, he should pour them out at the āstāva with the verses beginning with 'āpo hi ṣṭhā' ('Waters, you indeed are...').
When the sixth day has concluded, they should speak little and not study [the Veda] until the commencement of the next day.
He should feed the officiating priests with clarified butter and honey in multi-day sacrifices;
with clarified butter alone at the third pressing in sacrificial sessions.
In either of these two triduums, having chanted the pṛṣṭha laud, they should consume the soma of the atigrāhya cups;
and elsewhere, at this time, [they should consume] whatever they bring.
Everywhere the pṛṣṭhya [ṣaḍaha] should be accompanied by the prescribed rules,

sanskrit_iast: āmīvarttastotrīyānābhiplavikān pṛṣṭhye śaṃsayedbrāhmaṇāchesinā kāleyarco'cchāvākena sarvvatra yadā pavamāne syātām
meaning: आमीवर्त्तस्तोत्रीयानाभिप्लविकान् पृष्ठ्ये शंसयेद्ब्राह्मणाछेसिना कालेयर्चोऽच्छावाकेन सर्व्वत्र यदा पवमाने स्याताम्

text_mt: Everywhere [he should cause] the indrakratu [verses to be recited] by the brāhmaṇācchaṃsin priest after the Viṣuvant day and before the atirātra sacrifice.
In the Viśvajit sacrifice, he should perform the prescribed rules for the Vairāja laud.
Even in the case of the other pṛṣṭha lauds, according to the teachers' opinion.
On the seventh day, the Agner arka and the adhyardheḍa Somasāma are upon the first two verses of the maukṣa [sāman];
or the maukṣa and Somasāma are upon the subsequent two verses of the gāyatra, and the Agner arka is upon the three [verses];
some interchange the two saṃkṣāra cadences of the Sākamaśva and Iḍā [sāmans];
some [place] the Surūpa and Krauñca [sāmans] on two single verses.
The final chant of the ninth [day] is the Jyotiṣṭoma;
Upon its bṛhatī verse are the forest-sung melodies upon triplets, as well as the pṛṣṭhya [sāman];
the Vāsiṣṭha [sāman] is upon the intercalated verse;
the Vaiyaśva [sāman] before the Bharga; the Ābhīśava before the Yaśas;
only seven [melodies] upon triplets, 'by which we may avoid repetition,' according to another [authority];
the final one is the Dīrghatamasaḥ Arka or the Sāmarāja;
upon the two subsequent verses of the pṛṣṭha laud are the Dīrghatamasaḥ Arka and the Māṇḍava; and the Aiḍasāmarāja is the final one.

sanskrit_iast: daśamasya bahiṣpavamānaṃ dvitīyaprabhṛtīnāṃ pañcānāmahnāmanurūpāḥ prathamācca bahiṣpavamānaṃ tannavarcam
meaning: दशमस्य बहिष्पवमानं द्वितीयप्रभृतीनां पञ्चानामह्नामनुरूपाः प्रथमाच्च बहिष्पवमानं तन्नवर्चम्
title: atha saptamī kaṇḍikā
text_mt: The bahiṣpavamāna chant of the tenth day consists of the corresponding verses of the five days beginning with the second, and the bahiṣpavamāna chant from the first day; it comprises nine verses.

sanskrit_iast: anurūpeṣu tṛcāḥ pratilomā ṛco navarca iti gautamaḥ
meaning: अनुरूपेषु तृचाः प्रतिलोमा ऋचो नवर्च इति गौतमः
text_mt: Gautama says: 'Triplets in the corresponding verses, and the verses in inverted order in the nine-verse laud.'
Dhānañjayya says: 'Triplets everywhere.'
Śāṇḍilyāyana says: 'The nine-verse laud should be as traditionally taught.'
Śāṇḍilya says: 'The verses are in inverted order everywhere.'
On this day, they should express an unexpressed [composition], rendering it in the measure of an anuṣṭubh.
In a longer meter, they should elide syllables; in a shorter one, they should repeat [syllables].

sanskrit_iast: agniṣṭomasāmnā stutvā prāk patnīsaṃyājebhyo yadebhiḥ prastute parārdhyaṃ vrajit syāttadgatvā pratyāvrajya manasānutsāhe huteṣu patnīsaṃyājeṣu gārhapatya udgātā juhuyādupasṛjandharuṇaṃ mātre mātaraṃ dharuṇo dhayan rāyaṣpoṣamiṣamūrjamasmāsu dīdharatsvāheti pūrvam
meaning: अग्निष्टोमसाम्ना स्तुत्वा प्राक् पत्नीसंयाजेभ्यो यदेभिः प्रस्तुते परार्ध्यं व्रजित् स्यात्तद्गत्वा प्रत्याव्रज्य मनसानुत्साहे हुतेषु पत्नीसंयाजेषु गार्हपत्य उद्गाता जुहुयादुपसृजन्धरुणं मात्रे मातरं धरुणो धयन् रायष्पोषमिषमूर्जमस्मासु दीधरत्स्वाहेति पूर्वम्
text_mt: Having chanted with the agniṣṭomasāman, before the patnīsaṃyāja offerings, if in their performance of the prastāva there should be a going to the furthest limit, having gone there and returned, if mentally unwilling, when the patnīsaṃyājas have been offered, the udgātṛ priest should offer [an oblation] in the gārhapatya fire, reciting the former formula: 'Releasing the offspring to the mother, the suckling suckling the mother, let wealth, increase, food, and sap be maintained in us, svāhā.'

sanskrit_iast: āhavanīyaṃ gatvā paścāttiṣṭhanto'yaṃ sahohā iti trirudgātā gāyet nidhanamitarāvanūpeyātām
meaning: आहवनीयं गत्वा पश्चात्तिष्ठन्तोऽयं सहोहा इति त्रिरुद्गाता गायेत् निधनमितरावनूपेयाताम्
text_mt: Having gone to the āhavanīya fire and standing behind it, the udgātṛ priest should sing thrice: 'ayaṃ sahohā'; the other two should join in with the cadence.

sanskrit_iast: yajamānasañcareṇa gatvā pūrvayā dvārā sadaḥ praviśeyuḥ
meaning: यजमानसञ्चरेण गत्वा पूर्वया द्वारा सदः प्रविशेयुः
text_mt: Proceeding along the pathway of the patron of the sacrifice, they should enter the sadas by the eastern door.

sanskrit_iast: yadā adhvaryurupākuryyādatha mānasena stuvīrannāyaṃ gauḥ pṛśnirakramīditi gāyatreṇa pṛthak stotrīyābhyo hiṃkāraṃ trikena stomenāstomayogā yajamānavācanena
meaning: यदा अध्वर्युरुपाकुर्य्यादथ मानसेन स्तुवीरन्नायं गौः पृश्निरक्रमीदिति गायत्रेण पृथक् स्तोत्रीयाभ्यो हिंकारं त्रिकेन स्तोमेनास्तोमयोगा यजमानवाचनेन
title: atha aṣṭamī kaṇḍikā
text_mt: When the adhvaryu priest has commenced, they should then chant the mental laud with the gāyatra melody on 'ayaṃ gauḥ pṛśnir akramīt' ('This spotted bull has stepped forth'), uttering the hiṅkāra syllable separately from the strophic verses, with a stoma of three verses, without the yoking of the stoma, through the recitation of the patron of the sacrifice.
At the moment of the pratihāra, the pratihārtṛ priest should exhale.
Having introduced the final [verse], he should look at the hotṛ priest, saying, 'This is it.'
They should perform everything in this stotra mentally,
indicating [it] by looking [at each other].

sanskrit_iast: yamadhvaryurbhakṣaṃ prayacchan manyeta tasya manasopahūya kastvā kaṃ bhakṣayāmīti bhakṣayeyuḥ
meaning: यमध्वर्युर्भक्षं प्रयच्छन् मन्येत तस्य मनसोपहूय कस्त्वा कं भक्षयामीति भक्षयेयुः
text_mt: When the adhvaryu priest presents the portion, they should consider it, invite each other mentally, and consume [it with the formula]: “Who eats you? Whom do I eat?”
Regarding [the rule]: “They recite the theological dialogue,” they should recite the gāyatrī three times, says Dhānañjayya.
This refers to the caturhotṛ formula, says Gautama.
[It should be performed] as in the horse three-day rite, says Śāṇḍilya.

sanskrit_iast: etasyāṃ velāyāṃ varān vṛṇīran manasā yāniccheyuḥ
meaning: एतस्यां वेलायां वरान् वृणीरन् मनसा यानिच्छेयुः
text_mt: At this time, they should mentally choose whatever boons they desire.

sanskrit_iast: uttarata udgātaudumbarīṃ gṛhṇīyāt paścāt pratiharttā dakṣiṇato brahmā purastāditare sarve
meaning: उत्तरत उद्गातौदुम्बरीं गृह्णीयात् पश्चात् प्रतिहर्त्ता दक्षिणतो ब्रह्मा पुरस्तादितरे सर्वे
text_mt: The udgātṛ priest should grasp the audumbarī pillar to the north, the pratihārtṛ priest to the west, the brahman to the south, and all the others to the east.

sanskrit_iast: atha japeyuriha dhṛtiriha svadhṛtiriha rantiriha ramadhvaṃ mayi dhṛtirmayi svadhṛtirmayi ramo mayi ramadhvamiti vā
meaning: अथ जपेयुरिह धृतिरिह स्वधृतिरिह रन्तिरिह रमध्वं मयि धृतिर्मयि स्वधृतिर्मयि रमो मयि रमध्वमिति वा
text_mt: Then they should whisper: “Here is support, here is self-support, here is delight, here find delight!” or “In me is support, in me is self-support, in me is delight, in me find delight!”
Restraining their speech and having closed the two doors, they should sit until the announcement of the stars.

sanskrit_iast: prokte nakṣatre pūrvayā dvārā niṣkramya subrahmaṇyāpraṇavairvācaṃ visṛjeranniti dhānañjayyaḥ
meaning: प्रोक्ते नक्षत्रे पूर्वया द्वारा निष्क्रम्य सुब्रह्मण्याप्रणवैर्वाचं विसृजेरन्निति धानञ्जय्यः
text_mt: When the stars have been announced, having exited through the eastern door, they should release their speech with the praṇava syllables of the subrahmaṇyā litany, says Dhānañjayya.
Just upon hearing [it] being called, says Śāṇḍilya.
In multi-day sacrifices, only the patron of the sacrifice should perform the choosing of boons and the restraint of speech.
The others, having performed [their parts], [act] according to need; having performed [their parts], [act] according to need.

sanskrit_iast: mahāvratasya pṛṣṭhya upākṛte yuktvā stomaṃ parimādo gāyediti bhāṇḍitāyanaḥ
meaning: महाव्रतस्य पृष्ठ्य उपाकृते युक्त्वा स्तोमं परिमादो गायेदिति भाण्डितायनः
title: atha navamī kaṇḍikā
text_mt: When the pṛṣṭha laud of the Mahāvrata has been brought near, having yoked the stoma, he should sing the parimād chants, says Bhāṇḍitāyana.
Having accepted the two blades of grass, without having yoked [the stoma], say Gautama, Śāṇḍilya, and Dhānañjayya.
Even before the bringing near of the stotra, say some.
Having gone south of the āgnīdhra shed, they should attend upon [the altar] north of the fire with [the formulas] beginning with “breath”; that is stated by the Brāhmaṇa.
The udgātṛ priest should sing each [parimād chant] once.
The other two should join in with the cadence,
In those that have stobhas at the beginning and the end, he should insert a stobha for each quarter-verse.
Having returned along the same way, [they attend upon] the tail [of the bird-altar].
[Passing] east of the two wings of the rite, [they attend upon] the southern wing.
They should attend upon the northern shoulder-joint.
He should modify the Vasiṣṭhanihava chant with “Viśve Devāḥ…”
Having attended upon the pit, having gone north of the āgnīdhra shed, standing behind [it],
facing west right from there, says Dhānañjayya.
They should join in with its final cadence until exhaustion of breath.
[They stand] east of the two cart-sheds, in front, facing west.

sanskrit_iast: tata evekṣamāṇā mārjālīyaṃ yat dvandveṣu nāke suparṇamiti
meaning: तत एवेक्षमाणा मार्जालीयं यत् द्वन्द्वेषु नाके सुपर्णमिति
text_mt: Looking from that very place at the mārjālīya hearth, [he sings] the verse “The fair-winged bird in the sky…” among the pairs.
As [they did] with the two cart-sheds, so with the sadas.
Standing within the sacrificial altar facing west, [they attend upon] the gārhapatya fire, says Dhānañjayya.
Standing behind it, says Śāṇḍilya.
They should join in directly at the cadence beginning with “Indra”.
There should be at least two chariots following him.
East of the sacrificial ground, the others should arm themselves apart from him.

sanskrit_iast: pūrveṇa patnīśālāmudgātā gatvā dakṣiṇe vedyante prāñco darbhānāstīryya teṣvenaṃ prāṅmukhamupaveśayet
meaning: पूर्वेण पत्नीशालामुद्गाता गत्वा दक्षिणे वेद्यन्ते प्राञ्चो दर्भानास्तीर्य्य तेष्वेनं प्राङ्मुखमुपवेशयेत्
text_mt: Having gone east of the wife's hall, the udgātṛ priest, having strewn eastward-pointing darbha grass at the southern edge of the altar, should seat him upon it facing east.

sanskrit_iast: athāsmai varmmābhiharedanyaṃ vābhiharantamanumantrayeta uttiṣṭha rājan parivarmmāsyaśca yukto ratho vitato daiva ākhaṇoviśāṃ rājā brāhmaṇa edhi gopteti
meaning: अथास्मै वर्म्माभिहरेदन्यं वाभिहरन्तमनुमन्त्रयेत उत्तिष्ठ राजन् परिवर्म्मास्यश्च युक्तो रथो विततो दैव आखणोविशां राजा ब्राह्मण एधि गोप्तेति
text_mt: Then he should bring armor to him, or consecrate another person bringing it [with the mantra]: “Arise, O king, put on armor; the chariot is yoked with horses, the divine target is stretched out; O king of the people, be a protector of the brāhmaṇa!”

sanskrit_iast: paścimena pariyāhītyuktvā tenaiva pratyāvrajyottara enaṃ vedyante'vasthāpya brūyād hastatraṃ badhnīṣvojyamāyudhaṃ kuruṣva trīniṣūnupakalpayasvāyasmāyānyameva kañca caturthamiti
meaning: पश्चिमेन परियाहीत्युक्त्वा तेनैव प्रत्याव्रज्योत्तर एनं वेद्यन्तेऽवस्थाप्य ब्रूयाद् हस्तत्रं बध्नीष्वोज्यमायुधं कुरुष्व त्रीनिषूनुपकल्पयस्वायस्मायान्यमेव कञ्च चतुर्थमिति
text_mt: Having said, “Drive around by the west,” having returned along the same way and stationed him at the northern edge of the altar, he should say: “Fasten the hand-guard, make your weapon strong, prepare three iron-headed arrows and any fourth [arrow]!”
He should say: “Fit [an arrow to the bow]!”

sanskrit_iast: taṃ pratidadhānamanumantrayeta vaiṇāvatāya pratidhatsva śaṃkumāpapro'ṣṭamo teti papradbrahmaṇo guptyaividhṛtyai dhārayātreti
meaning: तं प्रतिदधानमनुमन्त्रयेत वैणावताय प्रतिधत्स्व शंकुमापप्रोऽष्टमो तेति पप्रद्ब्रह्मणो गुप्त्यैविधृत्यै धारयात्रेति
text_mt: As he fits it, he should consecrate him [with the mantra]: “Fit the peg to the bow of bamboo; it has filled the eighth [part]; it has filled; for the protection of the brāhmaṇa, for maintenance, hold fast here!”
He should say: “Stand firm, closely gathered!”

sanskrit_iast: dakṣiṇena rathapathaṃ kṛtvottareṇāgnīdhrīyaṃ pūrvāpare carmaṇī vibadhnīyuḥ
meaning: दक्षिणेन रथपथं कृत्वोत्तरेणाग्नीध्रीयं पूर्वापरे चर्मणी विबध्नीयुः
text_mt: Having made a chariot path to the south, north of the āgnīdhra shed they should fasten two hides, one to the east and one to the west.

sanskrit_iast: taṃ brūyāt pradakṣiṇaṃ devayajanaṃ parīyāt pūrvañcarmāgamaneṣu vidhyerekaikenottarottaryanatipātayan
meaning: तं ब्रूयात् प्रदक्षिणं देवयजनं परीयात् पूर्वञ्चर्मागमनेषु विध्येरेकैकेनोत्तरोत्तर्यनतिपातयन्
text_mt: He should say to him: “Go clockwise around the sacrificial ground; pierce the eastern hide on your approaches, with one [arrow] after another, not shooting past [it]!”
The others should shoot at the western [hide] as they please.
[He should say]: “Having pierced [it] with the third [arrow], proceed north;
then shoot the fourth arrow in whichever direction you choose; having seen the cows, come to a halt;
there they should divest you of your armor.”
[he should instruct:] “Have this done at the time of the hiṅkāra syllable.”
He should proceed to the earth-drum.

title: atha ekādaśī kaṇḍikā
text_mt: West of the āgnīdhra shed, half of the pit of the [earth-]drum should be inside the sacrificial altar and half outside the sacrificial altar.
It should be covered with a bull's hide with the hair facing upwards.

sanskrit_iast: tvaṃ vāgasi ye naḥ satre anindiṣurdīkṣāyāśrānta āsite rāddhintebhyo dundubhe rāddhimasmabhyamāvadeti parāvada dviṣantaṃ ghorāṃ vācaṃ parāvadāthāsmabhysumitriyāṃ vācaṃ dundubhe kalyāṇīṃ kīrttimāvadeti parāvada dviṣato vādyandurhārdo ye viṣūkuhothāsmabhyaṃ puṣṭiṃ rāddhiśriyamāvada dundubha ityenametaiḥ pṛthagāhatya bāladhānenānyaṃ bāghnantamanumantryāpa upaspṛśya paścāttiṣṭhanto'gnimupatiṣṭheran namaste gāyatrāya yatte puro yatte śiro namaste rathantarāya yatte dakṣiṇato yatte dakṣiṇaḥ pakṣo namaste bṛhate yatte uttarato yatte uttaraḥ pakṣo namaste yajñāyajñīyāya yatte paścādyatte pucche namaste vāmadevyāya yatte ātmā yatte madhyamityetaiḥ pṛthagaṅgānyanvartham
meaning: त्वं वागसि ये नः सत्रे अनिन्दिषुर्दीक्षायाश्रान्त आसिते राद्धिन्तेभ्यो दुन्दुभे राद्धिमस्मभ्यमावदेति परावद द्विषन्तं घोरां वाचं परावदाथास्मभ्य्सुमित्रियां वाचं दुन्दुभे कल्याणीं कीर्त्तिमावदेति परावद द्विषतो वाद्यन्दुर्हार्दो ये विषूकुहोथास्मभ्यं पुष्टिं राद्धिश्रियमावद दुन्दुभ इत्येनमेतैः पृथगाहत्य बालधानेनान्यं बाघ्नन्तमनुमन्त्र्याप उपस्पृश्य पश्चात्तिष्ठन्तोऽग्निमुपतिष्ठेरन् नमस्ते गायत्राय यत्ते पुरो यत्ते शिरो नमस्ते रथन्तराय यत्ते दक्षिणतो यत्ते दक्षिणः पक्षो नमस्ते बृहते यत्ते उत्तरतो यत्ते उत्तरः पक्षो नमस्ते यज्ञायज्ञीयाय यत्ते पश्चाद्यत्ते पुच्छे नमस्ते वामदेव्याय यत्ते आत्मा यत्ते मध्यमित्येतैः पृथगङ्गान्यन्वर्थम्

sanskrit_iast: atha samastena tasmaite subhoḥ subhavo bhūyāsma nāmāsi nāma bhūyāsamāvirasyāvirmmā kuru savitaḥ pramāsuvayāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ bhūtau sampaśyasi teṣvabhibhūyāsśriyaṃ mayi dhehīti
meaning: अथ समस्तेन तस्मैते सुभोः सुभवो भूयास्म नामासि नाम भूयासमाविरस्याविर्म्मा कुरु सवितः प्रमासुवयां मनुष्याणां भूतौ सम्पश्यसि तेष्वभिभूयास्श्रियं मयि धेहीति
text_mt: Then [they revere it] collectively: "To that one, to you, O gracious one, may we become well-faring! You are name, may I become name! You are manifest, make me manifest! O Savitṛ, impel me forward; in whatever prosperity of men you look upon, may I surpass them; place prosperity in me!"
Having revered [it], they should enter the sadas.

title: atha dvādaśī kaṇḍikā
text_mt: Through the western door, they should bring in an armchair made of udumbara wood, woven with muñja grass.
If udumbara is not available, [it should be made] of [any] sacrificial tree.
Its legs are a span in length; the other parts are a cubit in length.
Having carried it to the south of the udumbarī pillar, they should place it to the north of it.

sanskrit_iast: tāmuttareṇodgātā gatvā paścādupaviśya bhūmispṛśo'syāḥ pādānkṛtvā kūrcāvadhastādupohyābhimṛśedbṛhadrathantare te pūrvo pādau śyaitanaudhase aparau vairūpavairāje anūcī śākvararaivatetiraścī ityetaiḥ pṛthagaṅgānyanvartham
meaning: तामुत्तरेणोद्गाता गत्वा पश्चादुपविश्य भूमिस्पृशोऽस्याः पादान्कृत्वा कूर्चावधस्तादुपोह्याभिमृशेद्बृहद्रथन्तरे ते पूर्वो पादौ श्यैतनौधसे अपरौ वैरूपवैराजे अनूची शाक्वररैवतेतिरश्ची इत्येतैः पृथगङ्गान्यन्वर्थम्
text_mt: The udgātṛ priest, having gone to the north of it, having sat down behind it, having made its legs touch the ground, and having slipped two bundles of grass underneath, should touch it: "The bṛhat and rathantara are your two front legs, the śyaita and naudhasa your two rear legs, the vairūpa and vairāja the longitudinal sides, the śākvara and raivata the transverse sides"—thus [he touches] the limbs separately according to their respective significance.

sanskrit_iast: vivayanamālabhyarcaḥ prāñca ātānā yajūṣi tiryañcaḥ sāmānyāstāraṇ śrīrupabarhaṇaṃ vākovākyamatīrokā vāravantīysandhayo rājanamātmā pratiṣṭhā yajñāyajñīyamiti
meaning: विवयनमालभ्यर्चः प्राञ्च आताना यजूषि तिर्यञ्चः सामान्यास्तारण् श्रीरुपबर्हणं वाकोवाक्यमतीरोका वारवन्तीय्सन्धयो राजनमात्मा प्रतिष्ठा यज्ञायज्ञीयमिति
text_mt: Touching the weaving, [he recites]: "The ṛc verses are the warp pointing eastward, the yajus formulas the woof pointing crosswise, the sāmans the matting, prosperity the pillow, dialogue the slits, the vāravantīya melodies the joints, the rājana melody the body, the yajñāyajñīya melody the foundation."

sanskrit_iast: tāṃ mukhenorasā bāhubhyāmiti spṛṣṭvārohet vasavastvā gāyatreṇa chandasā rohantu tānanvadhirohāmi rājyāya rudrāstvā traiṣṭubhena chandasā rohantu tānanvadhirohāmi vairājyāyādityāstvā jāgatena chandasā rohantu tānanvadhirohāmi svārājyāya viśve tvā devā ānuṣṭubhena chandasā rohantu tānanvadhirohāmi sāmrājyāyeti
meaning: तां मुखेनोरसा बाहुभ्यामिति स्पृष्ट्वारोहेत् वसवस्त्वा गायत्रेण छन्दसा रोहन्तु तानन्वधिरोहामि राज्याय रुद्रास्त्वा त्रैष्टुभेन छन्दसा रोहन्तु तानन्वधिरोहामि वैराज्यायादित्यास्त्वा जागतेन छन्दसा रोहन्तु तानन्वधिरोहामि स्वाराज्याय विश्वे त्वा देवा आनुष्टुभेन छन्दसा रोहन्तु तानन्वधिरोहामि साम्राज्यायेति
text_mt: Having touched it with his mouth, with his chest, and with his arms, he should ascend it: "May the Vasus mount you with the gāyatrī metre; I mount after them for kingship! May the Rudras mount you with the triṣṭubh metre; I mount after them for supreme sovereignty! May the Ādityas mount you with the jagatī metre; I mount after them for self-rule! May the All-Gods mount you with the anuṣṭubh metre; I mount after them for universal empire!"

sanskrit_iast: athaitaireva devatā udasya rājaśabdañcāmunā tvā chandasā rohāmītyārohet
meaning: अथैतैरेव देवता उदस्य राजशब्दञ्चामुना त्वा छन्दसा रोहामीत्यारोहेत्
text_mt: Then, having omitted the deities and the word 'kingship' from these very [formulas], he should ascend with: "I mount you with such-and-such metre."
With [the metres] ending with the vairāja as fifth, says Gautama.

sanskrit_iast: āruhya japetsyonāmāsadsuṣadāmāsadaṃ namaste'stu mā mā hsiīriti
meaning: आरुह्य जपेत्स्योनामासद्सुषदामासदं नमस्तेऽस्तु मा मा ह्सिईरिति

text_mt: While he mounts, the praṣṭhī, the brahmā, and the gṛhapati should mount bundles of grass.

sanskrit_iast: āsandyā vyākhyātaṃ dravyaṃ vāṇasya dravyaṃ vāṇasya
meaning: आसन्द्या व्याख्यातं द्रव्यं वाणस्य द्रव्यं वाणस्य
text_mt: By [the description of] the armchair, the material of the vāṇa lute has been explained; the material of the vāṇa lute [has been explained].

title: caturthaḥ prapāṭhakaḥ — atha prathamā kaṇḍikā
text_mt: It should be covered with the red hide of an ox with the hair facing upwards.

sanskrit_iast: tasya daśasu paścācchidreṣu daśa daśa tantryo baddhāḥ syurmauñjyo dārbhyo vā
meaning: तस्य दशसु पश्चाच्छिद्रेषु दश दश तन्त्र्यो बद्धाः स्युर्मौञ्ज्यो दार्भ्यो वा
text_mt: In its ten holes at the back, ten strings each should be tied, made of muñja or darbha grass.
In three [holes], says Śāṇḍilya: thirty-four in the middle one, thirty-three each on both sides.
Having divided them in front into three parts, one by one, he should draw them up separately one above the other with: "bhūs, bhuvas, svar!"

sanskrit_iast: tamabhimṛśedvado vada vadā vadī vado vadoruḥ pṛthuḥ sugaḥ sugaṃ tvaḥ karmaḥ karaṇaḥ karaḥ karasyurabhīṣāṭcābhīṣāhī cābhimātihaścābhimātihā ca sāsahiśca sahīyāśca sahasvāśca sahamānāścodvayāśca bṛhadvayāśca savayāśca bṛhadvayāścaindrīṃ vācaṃ bṛhatīṃ viśvarūpāśatāyuṣīṃ pravada deva vāṇeti
meaning: तमभिमृशेद्वदो वद वदा वदी वदो वदोरुः पृथुः सुगः सुगं त्वः कर्मः करणः करः करस्युरभीषाट्चाभीषाही चाभिमातिहश्चाभिमातिहा च सासहिश्च सहीयाश्च सहस्वाश्च सहमानाश्चोद्वयाश्च बृहद्वयाश्च सवयाश्च बृहद्वयाश्चैन्द्रीं वाचं बृहतीं विश्वरूपाशतायुषीं प्रवद देव वाणेति
text_mt: He should touch it: "Speak, speak, speak, speak! Speak, wide, broad, easily traversed, easy path, action, maker, doing, active! You are both overpowering and conquering, slayer of foes and destroyer of rivals, enduring and superior, powerful and prevailing, soaring and soaring high, youthful and mature! Proclaim the great Indra-related speech, all-formed, giving a hundredfold lifespan, O divine vāṇa lute!"

sanskrit_iast: śithilāstantunā yachedebhirno vāṇa tantubhiḥ śataṃ rāddhīrihābahārātsma sarve'tārṣma jīvā jyotiraśīmahīti
meaning: शिथिलास्तन्तुना यछेदेभिर्नो वाण तन्तुभिः शतं राद्धीरिहाबहारात्स्म सर्वेऽतार्ष्म जीवा ज्योतिरशीमहीति
text_mt: He should tighten the loose strings: "With these strings, O vāṇa lute, bring a hundred successes here to us; we have all succeeded, we have crossed over alive, may we attain the light!"

sanskrit_iast: vāksarvaṃ mano jyotirmā no bhadra iti japitvā vādayedindreṇatayeṣīkayā vetasaśākhayā ca sapalāśayā mūlataḥ
meaning: वाक्सर्वं मनो ज्योतिर्मा नो भद्र इति जपित्वा वादयेदिन्द्रेणतयेषीकया वेतसशाखया च सपलाशया मूलतः
text_mt: Having whispered, "Speech is everything, the mind is light, may our welfare not [be lost]," he should play it from the base with an arrow reed and with a leafy branch of cane.
With "For out-breath, to you!" he should stroke upwards; with "For down-breath, to you!" downwards.

sanskrit_iast: vyānāya tvā vyānāya tveti triḥ saṃlikhyodañcaṃ prohet
meaning: व्यानाय त्वा व्यानाय त्वेति त्रिः संलिख्योदञ्चं प्रोहेत्
text_mt: Having stroked three times with "For through-breath, to you! For through-breath, to you!" he should push it northward,
having spoken to a brāhmaṇa: "Sit stroking this!"

sanskrit_iast: āhata dundubhīn pravadantu vīṇā iti brūyāt
meaning: आहत दुन्दुभीन् प्रवदन्तु वीणा इति ब्रूयात्
text_mt: He should say: "Beat the drums! Let the lutes sound!"

sanskrit_iast: alāvuvīṇāṃ vakrākapiśīrṣṭyau ca pūrvasyāṃ dvāri bahiḥsadasam
meaning: अलावुवीणां वक्राकपिशीर्ष्ट्यौ च पूर्वस्यां द्वारि बहिःसदसम्
title: atha dvitīyā kaṇḍikā
text_mt: A gourd-lute and the curved lute and monkey-headed lute [should be placed] at the eastern door outside the sadas.

sanskrit_iast: vakrākapiśīrṣṭyau dundubhīśca pratimantrayeta yā vakrāyāṃ kapiśīrṣyyāṃ dundubhau yacca vādyaṃ ghoṣo yo mahato mahāstena norāddhi māvadeti
meaning: वक्राकपिशीर्ष्ट्यौ दुन्दुभीश्च प्रतिमन्त्रयेत या वक्रायां कपिशीर्ष्य्यां दुन्दुभौ यच्च वाद्यं घोषो यो महतो महास्तेन नोराद्धि मावदेति
text_mt: He should address the curved lute, the monkey-headed lute, and the drums: "Whatever musical sound is in the curved lute, in the monkey-headed lute, and in the drum, which great sound belongs to the great, with that proclaim success to us!"
And the great lute and piśīla lute [should be placed] at the western [door]—inside, say Gautama and Śāṇḍilya; outside, says Dhānañjayya.

sanskrit_iast: alābuvīṇāpi śīlavīṇe ca pratimantrayetālābuvīṇe'pi śīlī ca yaṃ mantramadhijagmatustenedamupagāyatāṃ te sāmamahayeṣyata iti
meaning: अलाबुवीणापि शीलवीणे च प्रतिमन्त्रयेतालाबुवीणेऽपि शीली च यं मन्त्रमधिजग्मतुस्तेनेदमुपगायतां ते साममहयेष्यत इति
text_mt: He should address the gourd-lute and piśīla lute: "Whatever formula the gourd-lute and piśīlī have attained, with that let this [lute] sing along; your sāman shall be magnified!"

sanskrit_iast: paścimenopagātṝn dve dve ekaikā patnī kāṇḍavīṇāṃ pichorāñca vyatyāsaṃ vādayet
meaning: पश्चिमेनोपगातॄन् द्वे द्वे एकैका पत्नी काण्डवीणां पिछोराञ्च व्यत्यासं वादयेत्
text_mt: Behind the choristers, each wife should play two [instruments] each in turn: a reed lute and a picchorā.
The picchorā near her mouth, the reed lute by plucking.
These they call apaghāṭilās.

sanskrit_iast: tāḥ pratimantrayeta yāṃ patnyapaghāṭilāṃ mṛdukaṃ vādayiṣyati sārātimapavādhatāṃ dviṣantaṃ taijanitvagiti
meaning: ताः प्रतिमन्त्रयेत यां पत्न्यपघाटिलां मृदुकं वादयिष्यति सारातिमपवाधतां द्विषन्तं तैजनित्वगिति
text_mt: He should address them: "Whatever apaghāṭilā the wife will play softly, may it ward off malice, [ward off] the enemy with its sharp skin!"

sanskrit_iast: sarvamanuvīkṣamāṇo japedākrandā ulūlayaḥ prakośā yavācaṣṭati sarvā satrasya sā rāddhistathedsāma gīyata iti
meaning: सर्वमनुवीक्षमाणो जपेदाक्रन्दा उलूलयः प्रकोशा यवाचष्टति सर्वा सत्रस्य सा राद्धिस्तथेद्साम गीयत इति
text_mt: Looking around at everything, he should whisper: "The cries, the ululations, the clamorous shouts that have sounded, all that is the success of the sacrificial session; so is this sāman sung!"

sanskrit_iast: japedeva suparṇo'smi garutmān premāṃ vācaṃ vadiṣyāmi bahu kariṣyantīṃ bahu kariṣyan svargamayiṣyantīṃ svargamayiṣyan māmimān yajamānāniti
meaning: जपेदेव सुपर्णोऽस्मि गरुत्मान् प्रेमां वाचं वदिष्यामि बहु करिष्यन्तीं बहु करिष्यन् स्वर्गमयिष्यन्तीं स्वर्गमयिष्यन् मामिमान् यजमानानिति
text_mt: He should whisper: "I am the fair-winged bird, Garutmān; I shall speak forth this speech that is to bring abundance, bringing abundance [to myself], and that is to bring to heaven, bringing to heaven me and these patrons of the sacrifice!"

sanskrit_iast: brāhmaṇo'bhigaraḥ pūrvasyā sadaso dvāri pratyaṅmukha upaviśet
meaning: ब्राह्मणोऽभिगरः पूर्वस्या सदसो द्वारि प्रत्यङ्मुख उपविशेत्
title: atha tṛtīyā kaṇḍikā
text_mt: A brāhmaṇa praiser should sit at the eastern door of the sadas facing west.
A low-caste decrier [should sit] at the western [door] facing east.
He should say: "These participants in the sacrificial session have not succeeded!"

sanskrit_iast: dakṣiṇena mārjālīyamaryo'ntarvedi dakṣiṇāmukhastiṣṭhet bahirvedi śūdra udaṅmukhaḥ
meaning: दक्षिणेन मार्जालीयमर्योऽन्तर्वेदि दक्षिणामुखस्तिष्ठेत् बहिर्वेदि शूद्र उदङ्मुखः
text_mt: To the south of the mārjālīya hearth, an Ārya should stand within the sacrificial enclosure facing south; a Śūdra outside the sacrificial enclosure facing north.
In the absence of an Ārya [vaiśya], anyone of an Āryan caste [may stand].
The two should pull at a white circular hide,
To the east of the Āgnīdhra [hearth], a Vedic student should stand inside the sacrificial enclosure facing north, and a courtesan outside the sacrificial enclosure facing south.
She should say: 'You ill-behaved breaker of the vow of chastity!'

sanskrit_iast: dhiktvā jālmi puṃścali grāmasya mārjani puruṣasya puruṣasya śiśnapraṇejanīti brahmacārī
meaning: धिक्त्वा जाल्मि पुंश्चलि ग्रामस्य मार्जनि पुरुषस्य पुरुषस्य शिश्नप्रणेजनीति ब्रह्मचारी
text_mt: The Vedic student [should say]: 'Fie upon you, wretched courtesan, the cleanser of the village, the washer of every man's penis!'
Thus [they exchange insults] alternately up to the third time.
When the rite of all [the others] is completed, the laudatory reciter should say just that three times.
Having let go, the śūdra should run away.
He should strike him with that very [skin].
The Vedic student should revile the other woman as desired.

sanskrit_iast: paścimenāgnīdhrīyaṃ bahirvedi pariśrite mithunau sambhavetāṃ yau varṇau labheran
meaning: पश्चिमेनाग्नीध्रीयं बहिर्वेदि परिश्रिते मिथुनौ सम्भवेतां यौ वर्णौ लभेरन्
text_mt: To the west of the Āgnīdhra [hearth], outside the sacrificial enclosure in an enclosed space, a couple should unite sexually, of whichever castes they may obtain.

sanskrit_iast: gṛhapaterdāsyo navānudaharaṇānpūrayitvā pradakṣiṇaṃ mārjālīyaṃ parīyurhaimahā3idaṃ madhvidaṃ madhviti vadatyaḥ pañcāvarārddhyāḥ pañcaśatamparārddhyāḥ pañcavśitiḥ sāmpratāḥ
meaning: गृहपतेर्दास्यो नवानुदहरणान्पूरयित्वा प्रदक्षिणं मार्जालीयं परीयुर्हैमहा3इदं मध्विदं मध्विति वदत्यः पञ्चावरार्द्ध्याः पञ्चशतम्परार्द्ध्याः पञ्चव्शितिः साम्प्रताः
text_mt: Female slaves of the householder, having filled new water-jars, should walk around the Mārjālīya [hearth] from left to right, saying: 'O Great One! This is honey! This is honey!'—five at least, fifty at most, twenty-five being proper.
They should fasten war drums at all the corners.
They should utter speeches of ever higher and higher pitch, as many as they can find.
Following the hiṅkāra syllable, the laudatory reciters and others, having performed [their parts], should act according to need.
Until the end of the stotra, the women carrying water pitchers and all the noises [should continue].

sanskrit_iast: caturviśena vā stutvā madhyamāmahiṃkṛtāṃ tṛcasya prastuyāt
meaning: चतुर्विशेन वा स्तुत्वा मध्यमामहिंकृतां तृचस्य प्रस्तुयात्
text_mt: Or, having chanted with twenty-four [verses], he should chant the middle [verse] of the triplet without a hiṅkāra syllable as the prastāva.
One should not do that, says Śāṇḍilyāyana.

sanskrit_iast: uttamāyāṃ stotrīyāyāmastutāyāṃ pādāvupāvaharet sahanidhanena bhūmau pratiṣṭhāpayet
meaning: उत्तमायां स्तोत्रीयायामस्तुतायां पादावुपावहरेत् सहनिधनेन भूमौ प्रतिष्ठापयेत्
text_mt: While the final strophic verse is still unchanted, he should lower his two feet; together with the cadence, he should set them firmly on the ground.

sanskrit_iast: āhriyamāṇe bhakṣe pratilomairārohaṇīyairavaruhya japenmahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca na imaṃ yajñammimikṣatāṃ pipṛtānno bharīmabhiriti
meaning: आह्रियमाणे भक्षे प्रतिलोमैरारोहणीयैरवरुह्य जपेन्मही द्यौः पृथिवी च न इमं यज्ञम्मिमिक्षतां पिपृतान्नो भरीमभिरिति
text_mt: While the portion is being brought, stepping down by the mounting-steps in reverse order, he should mutter: 'May the great Heaven and Earth sprinkle this our sacrifice, and satisfy us with fosterings!'
Seated below, they should chant with the remainder [of the verses].
When the concluding atirātra sacrifice is finished, they should go down to the concluding purificatory bath without immersing themselves completely.
They should rub each other clean with their hands.
He whose wife is present there should have his back rubbed clean by her.
Having come up, the householder should put on the cloth used for wrapping soma.
They should conclude [the rite] starting with the sprinkling.
By whichever way they went out from here, they should return by another.

sanskrit_iast: anūbandhyavapāyāṃ hutāyāṃ dakṣiṇe vedyante keśaśmaśrūṇi vāpayeran
meaning: अनूबन्ध्यवपायां हुतायां दक्षिणे वेद्यन्ते केशश्मश्रूणि वापयेरन्
text_mt: When the omentum of the post-sacrificial barren cow has been offered, they should have their hair and beards shaved at the southern edge of the altar.

sanskrit_iast: tasmin ssthite prācca udañco vā gatvā pṛthagudavasānīyābhiriṣṭibhirāhitāgnayo yajeran
meaning: तस्मिन् स्स्थिते प्राच्च उदञ्चो वा गत्वा पृथगुदवसानीयाभिरिष्टिभिराहिताग्नयो यजेरन्
text_mt: When that is completed, going east or north, those who have established their sacred fires should sacrifice separately with the concluding departing oblations.
Those who have not established their sacred fires should wait upon the householder as their sacrificer.
They should sacrifice with cooked mess offerings dedicated to those deities: thus [holds] Dhānañjayya.
or for twelve nights, or for a day and a night,
or for as long as they pressed soma, or for as long as they pressed soma.

title: atha pañcamī kaṇḍikā
text_mt: Now then follow the alternatives for the Gavāmayana.
Some perform the entire [sacrifice] on the model of the jyotiṣṭoma.
Or the atirātra, the twenty-four-fold day, the nine-day period, the mahāvrata, and the atirātra should remain in their proper places, and the rest [is performed] on the model of the jyotiṣṭoma.

sanskrit_iast: atra vā goāyuṣī pṛṣṭhyābhiplavau daśarātramityupāharet sa saṃvatsarapravarhaḥ
meaning: अत्र वा गोआयुषी पृष्ठ्याभिप्लवौ दशरात्रमित्युपाहरेत् स संवत्सरप्रवर्हः
text_mt: Or here, one should introduce the Go and Āyus days, the pṛṣṭhya and abhiplava six-day periods, and the ten-day period: that is the 'pulling out' of the year.
'We arrange with various days', as this Brāhmaṇa says.
When making the atirātra sacrifice possess both sāmans, after the Āndhīgava melody come the Audala and Bṛhat melodies; if there is a ṣoḍaśin, the Nānada melody takes the place of the Audala.
The sāman triplet of the Bṛhat is placed prior.
Some perform the twenty-four-fold day without the Rathantara melody.
Or having the Rathantara melody for the pṛṣṭha laud, with the Bṛhat melody set to an anuṣṭubh verse.
Some arrange the abhiplava and svarasāman days according to the ritual paradigm of the jyotiṣṭoma.
That being so, the Śāṭyāyanins adapt the distributions of the six-day period accordingly.

sanskrit_iast: dvividhamabhiplavameka upavatyagriyavatī ca vyatyāsampratipadau rāthantarabārhatāni cājyāni
meaning: द्विविधमभिप्लवमेक उपवत्यग्रियवती च व्यत्यासम्प्रतिपदौ राथन्तरबार्हतानि चाज्यानि
text_mt: Some consider the abhiplava to be of two kinds: alternating the opening verses containing upa and containing agriya, and the ājya lauds based on the Rathantara and Bṛhat melodies.

sanskrit_iast: ājyapratipadāvauśanakāve antye pārthayāme vā bārhatānāṃ svayonyabhībartto rathantarapṛṣṭheṣu śyaitarkṣu bṛhatpṛṣṭheṣu
meaning: आज्यप्रतिपदावौशनकावे अन्त्ये पार्थयामे वा बार्हतानां स्वयोन्यभीबर्त्तो रथन्तरपृष्ठेषु श्यैतर्क्षु बृहत्पृष्ठेषु
text_mt: The two introductory verses of the ājyastotras are the auśana chant and the kāva chant; on the final [days], or the pārthayāma chant; of the bārhata days, the abhīvarta chant on its own womb-verse [is used]; in the rathantara-pṛṣṭha days, the śyaita chant; on verses in the bṛhat-pṛṣṭha days.
Its bahiṣpavamāna chant on the first day is from the unshifted (samūḍha).
Some [prescribe] the unshifted [order] having the rathantara and bṛhat as pṛṣṭha lauds.

sanskrit_iast: nānāpṛṣṭhe cottare caturahe rathantarabṛhatī vyatyāsampavamāneṣu bṛhatīṣu rathantaramanuṣṭupsu bṛhate dvitīye
meaning: नानापृष्ठे चोत्तरे चतुरहे रथन्तरबृहती व्यत्यासम्पवमानेषु बृहतीषु रथन्तरमनुष्टुप्सु बृहते द्वितीये
text_mt: And in the four following days having diverse pṛṣṭhas, the rathantara and the bṛhat alternate in the pavamāna chants: on bṛhatī verses the rathantara, on anuṣṭubh verses the bṛhat, on the second [day].
Before the chant with the āṣkāra cadence [is inserted] the kaulmalabarhiṣa chant.
Before the āndhīgava chant, the śyāvāśva chant.

title: atha ṣaṣṭhī kaṇḍikā
text_mt: The bṛhatī verse beginning with the ānūpa verse is on the fifth [day].
Before the mānava chant, the hārāyaṇa chant.
Before the chant with the madhuścyut cadence, the ākūpāra chant.
Before the bṛhat are three single verses.
And on the sixth day, [subsequent] to the bṛhat, in the shifted [order].
And the two śaśakarṇa chants are constant in the third pṛṣṭhya day.
One should arrange the abhīvarta and the kāleya chants on bṛhatī verses, so says Gautama.
One should not adapt the shifted [order], so says Śāṇḍilyāyana.

sanskrit_iast: ekavśityahakāriṇa upariṣṭādabhijitaḥ pṛṣṭyamupayanti prāk ca viśvajitaḥ svarasāmnaścokthyān
meaning: एकव्शित्यहकारिण उपरिष्टादभिजितः पृष्ट्यमुपयन्ति प्राक् च विश्वजितः स्वरसाम्नश्चोक्थ्यान्
text_mt: Those who perform the twenty-one-day rite undertake the pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha after the abhijit day and before the viśvajit day, and the svara-sāman days as ukthya sacrifices.
Some transpose the abhijit and the viśvajit days.

sanskrit_iast: abhijito rathantarapṛṣṭhasya rāthantarī pratipaddhoturājyañcābhivāyumityauśanaṃ jyotiṣṭomaṃ par sujñānamuṣṇihi śyāvāśvāt pūrve gaurīvitabṛhatī
meaning: अभिजितो रथन्तरपृष्ठस्य राथन्तरी प्रतिपद्धोतुराज्यञ्चाभिवायुमित्यौशनं ज्योतिष्टोमं पर् सुज्ञानमुष्णिहि श्यावाश्वात् पूर्वे गौरीवितबृहती
text_mt: For the abhijit day having the rathantara-pṛṣṭha, the introductory verse belongs to the rathantara, and the hotṛ's ājyastotra is on "abhivāyum"; the auśana chant; the jyotiṣṭoma beyond; the sujñāna chant on the uṣṇih verse; before the śyāvāśva chant are the gaurīvita and the bṛhatī chants.
Some [prescribe] the rathantara and the bṛhat on their own womb-verses in the svara-sāman days.

sanskrit_iast: svarapṛṣṭhāścetsvārasāmikeṣu pṛṣṭhastotrīyeṣu yathāsv svārāṇi cārbhavāntyāni dvaigatagautamayoḥ sthāne rathantaramantarikṣasya gautam svarasya vṛhatdvitīye nityaśca sāmatṛcaḥ
meaning: स्वरपृष्ठाश्चेत्स्वारसामिकेषु पृष्ठस्तोत्रीयेषु यथास्व् स्वाराणि चार्भवान्त्यानि द्वैगतगौतमयोः स्थाने रथन्तरमन्तरिक्षस्य गौतम् स्वरस्य वृहत्द्वितीये नित्यश्च सामतृचः
text_mt: If they have svara-pṛṣṭha chants: in the pṛṣṭha strophic verses of the svara-sāman days, according to their own svara chants, and the final chants of the third pressing; in place of the dvaigata and gautama chants, the rathantara; in place of the antarikṣa-gautama and the svara chant, the bṛhat; on the second [day], the regular chant triplet.
The exclusion of the audala and tvāṣṭrī sāmans [takes place].
Some perform the morning recitation for the viṣuvat day by day.
Some praise with the bahiṣpavamāna chant outside of it.
"agnirindrāya", "upāsmai pavasva vāce" are the strophic verses according to the Śuṅgas.
"vāta ā vātu" according to the Māṣaśarāvis.
Some transpose the yajñāyajñīya and the bhāsa chants.

sanskrit_iast: baṇmahāṃ asi sūryendramiddevatātaye śrāyantaiva sūryamiti mahādivākīrtyastotrīyā vikalpate
meaning: बण्महां असि सूर्येन्द्रमिद्देवतातये श्रायन्तैव सूर्यमिति महादिवाकीर्त्यस्तोत्रीया विकल्पते
text_mt: "baṇ mahām asi sūrya", "indram id devatātaye", "śrāyanta iva sūryam": thus the strophic verse of the mahādivākīrtya chant is optional.

sanskrit_iast: bṛhatpṛṣṭhaścedagriyavatī pratipattṛtīyāt sāhasrādājyāni nityairvikalpanta utsedhasthāne rathantaraṃ tasya mahādivākīrtyamaysoma iti pārthamābhijitāni pṛṣṭhānīndrakratau śyaitaṅgoḥ kakubuṣṇihāvuddharatipipīlikamadhyā śyāvāśvavikarṇagaurīvitāndhīgavaudalabhāsānyanuṣṭhubhyaudalasthāne vā vāṅnidhanaṃ krauñcamaraṇye geye tṛcayorvratātpare
meaning: बृहत्पृष्ठश्चेदग्रियवती प्रतिपत्तृतीयात् साहस्रादाज्यानि नित्यैर्विकल्पन्त उत्सेधस्थाने रथन्तरं तस्य महादिवाकीर्त्यमय्सोम इति पार्थमाभिजितानि पृष्ठानीन्द्रक्रतौ श्यैतङ्गोः ककुबुष्णिहावुद्धरतिपिपीलिकमध्या श्यावाश्वविकर्णगौरीवितान्धीगवौदलभासान्यनुष्ठुभ्यौदलस्थाने वा वाङ्निधनं क्रौञ्चमरण्ये गेये तृचयोर्व्रतात्परे
title: atha saptamī kaṇḍikā
text_mt: If it has the bṛhat as pṛṣṭha laud, the introductory verse contains the word "agriya"; the ājyastotras from the third sāhasra rite alternate with the constant ones; in place of the utsedha chant, the rathantara; its mahādivākīrtya chant; "ayam somaḥ" is the pārtha chant; the pṛṣṭha lauds of the abhijit day; in the indrakratu chant, the śyaita chant; he removes the kakubh and uṣṇih verses of the go-sāman; the pipīlikamadhyā verse; the śyāvāśva, vikarṇa, gaurīvita, āndhīgava, audala, and bhāsa chants on the anuṣṭubh verses, or in place of the audala chant the krauñca chant with the cadence "vāc"; in the forest-sung melody after the mahāvrata for the two triplets.
In the viśvajit day, some transpose the yajñāyajñīya and the bṛhatī chants.

sanskrit_iast: bṛhatpṛṣṭhaścettṛtīyāt sāhasrāt prātaḥsavanaṃ kāleyasthāne samantamābhijitāni pṛṣṭhānīndrakratau śyaitaṅgoḥ kakubuṣṇihāvuddharati pipīlikamadhyā anuṣṭupprabhṛti vratāt
meaning: बृहत्पृष्ठश्चेत्तृतीयात् साहस्रात् प्रातःसवनं कालेयस्थाने समन्तमाभिजितानि पृष्ठानीन्द्रक्रतौ श्यैतङ्गोः ककुबुष्णिहावुद्धरति पिपीलिकमध्या अनुष्टुप्प्रभृति व्रतात्
text_mt: If it has the bṛhat as pṛṣṭha laud, the morning pressing is from the third sāhasra rite; in place of the kāleya chant, the samanta chant; the pṛṣṭha lauds of the abhijit day; in the indrakratu chant, the śyaita chant; he removes the kakubh and uṣṇih verses of the go-sāman; the pipīlikamadhyā verse; beginning from the anuṣṭubh verse up to the mahāvrata.
Options for the course of the latter half [of the year].
Those who follow day-repetition undertake the abhiplava and pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍahas in reverse order.
Those who follow month-repetition [undertake] the pṛṣṭhya and abhiplava-ṣaḍahas in direct order.
And they invert the go and āyus days.

sanskrit_iast: uttamaṃ sambhāryyaṃ kurvan saptamānmāsān pṛṣṭhyābhiplavānuddharet pañcāyanamāsān kṛtvā daśarātramiśrādabhiplavamuddharet
meaning: उत्तमं सम्भार्य्यं कुर्वन् सप्तमान्मासान् पृष्ठ्याभिप्लवानुद्धरेत् पञ्चायनमासान् कृत्वा दशरात्रमिश्रादभिप्लवमुद्धरेत्
text_mt: Making the final [month] a composite, one should remove the pṛṣṭhya and abhiplava-ṣaḍahas from the seventh month; having made five course-months, one should remove the abhiplava-ṣaḍaha mixed with the daśarātra.
That being so, it is optional in the former half.
Having removed the abhiplava and pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍahas from the sixth [month], he should make them subsequent to the twenty-fourth [day].

sanskrit_iast: samau pakṣau cikīrṣan pañcāyanamāsān kṛtvā daśarātramiśraṃ māsamuddharet pañcadaśau pakṣau vratasyāparimātkaṃ bṛhatpṛṣṭhaṃ viśvajitam
meaning: समौ पक्षौ चिकीर्षन् पञ्चायनमासान् कृत्वा दशरात्रमिश्रं मासमुद्धरेत् पञ्चदशौ पक्षौ व्रतस्यापरिमात्कं बृहत्पृष्ठं विश्वजितम्
text_mt: Wishing to make both halves equal, having made five course-months, one should remove the month mixed with the daśarātra; two fifteen-day periods; not measuring around the mahāvrata; the viśvajit day having the bṛhat as pṛṣṭha laud.
Some undertake the āyus day after the viśvajit day.
That being so, the two bṛhatī verses of the go and āyus days belong to the one-day sacrifice.
Some repeat the ten-day period (daśarātra).

sanskrit_iast: tasmādvrataṃ yadā paraṃ vratānte mānasaṃ sāṃvargyajitā gotamāḥ
meaning: तस्माद्व्रतं यदा परं व्रतान्ते मानसं सांवर्ग्यजिता गोतमाः
text_mt: When the mahāvrata is subsequent to that, at the end of the mahāvrata [takes place] the mānasa chant, according to the Gotamas who have conquered through the saṃvargya chant.

title: atha aṣṭamī kaṇḍikā
text_mt: Options for the course of the stars (jyotiṣām ayana).
In that regard, whatever is from the beginning is at the end above the viṣuvat day.
Month by month, in place of the first abhiplava-ṣaḍaha, the trikadruka days [are used].

sanskrit_iast: sa ṣaṭtriṃśadūno nākṣatraḥ saptaviṃśino hi māsāḥ
meaning: स षट्त्रिंशदूनो नाक्षत्रः सप्तविंशिनो हि मासाः
text_mt: That [year] is deficient by thirty-six [days], [being] sidereal (nākṣatra), for the months consist of twenty-seven [days].

sanskrit_iast: ṣaṣṭhādyasyābhiplavasya sthāne jyotirgauśca jyotirevāvṛtte sa navono nākṣatra eva trayodaśī
meaning: षष्ठाद्यस्याभिप्लवस्य स्थाने ज्योतिर्गौश्च ज्योतिरेवावृत्ते स नवोनो नाक्षत्र एव त्रयोदशी
text_mt: In place of the first abhiplava-ṣaḍaha from the sixth, the jyotis and go days [are placed], and only the jyotis when inverted; that [year] is deficient by nine [days], the sidereal one [having] thirteen [months].
In the even months, in place of the first abhiplava-ṣaḍaha is that five-day period; that [year] is deficient by six [days], [being] lunar (cāndramasa).

sanskrit_iast: ṣaṣṭhādau trikadrukānabhiplavañcopadadhyāt so'ṣṭādaśādhikaḥ paurṇamāsī prasavastairyyagayanika ādityasya
meaning: षष्ठादौ त्रिकद्रुकानभिप्लवञ्चोपदध्यात् सोऽष्टादशाधिकः पौर्णमासी प्रसवस्तैर्य्यगयनिक आदित्यस्य
text_mt: At the beginning of the sixth [month] one should insert the trikadruka days and an abhiplava-ṣaḍaha; that has eighteen [days] in excess, having the full moon as impulse, belonging to the transverse course of the sun.
Just as is the end, so is the beginning of the inverted [periods].
In the former abhiplava-ṣaḍahas having made the sixth day an ukthya, [one makes it] an agniṣṭoma in the final one.

sanskrit_iast: asṛkṣateti bahiṣpavamānaṃ gāyatraṃ gāyatryāmāśvamaiḍe bṛhatyāṃ goṣṭho vāyā ruceti gāyatrapārśvamārbhavaḥ
meaning: असृक्षतेति बहिष्पवमानं गायत्रं गायत्र्यामाश्वमैडे बृहत्यां गोष्ठो वाया रुचेति गायत्रपार्श्वमार्भवः

sanskrit_iast: savanavidhaṃ paśuṃ kurvannuttamamabhiplavapañcāhaṃ kṛtvā ṣaṣṭhasthāne savanavidhaḥ paśuḥ
meaning: सवनविधं पशुं कुर्वन्नुत्तममभिप्लवपञ्चाहं कृत्वा षष्ठस्थाने सवनविधः पशुः
text_mt: Performing the animal sacrifice in accordance with the pressing, having made the final abhiplava a five-day period, the animal sacrifice in accordance with the pressing takes place in the position of the sixth [day].

sanskrit_iast: prathamañcābhiplavaṃ pañcāhaṃ kṛtvā māsānte savanavidhaḥ paśuḥ
meaning: प्रथमञ्चाभिप्लवं पञ्चाहं कृत्वा मासान्ते सवनविधः पशुः
text_mt: And having made the first abhiplava a five-day period, the animal sacrifice in accordance with the pressing takes place at the end of the month.
Some [teachers say] that they should make all [months] deficient, [making] the first abhiplava a five-day period.
Or they should combine the two contiguous days of the abhiplava and the pṛṣṭhya [periods].

sanskrit_iast: tathā satyekādaśyāṃ pūrvapakṣasya dīkṣitvā trayodaśadīkṣāḥ kurvīran
meaning: तथा सत्येकादश्यां पूर्वपक्षस्य दीक्षित्वा त्रयोदशदीक्षाः कुर्वीरन्
text_mt: If that is so, having consecrated themselves on the eleventh day of the bright fortnight, they should observe thirteen consecrations.
Or alternating [full and deficient months]: "Not full, nor deficient-full, from the recurring [month]," say the Śālaṅkāyanins.
Those consecrated on the Ekāṣṭakā day are subject to misfortune; they should sit silently on the thirty-first day.
Or they should sacrifice with an animal sacrifice in accordance with the pressing.

sanskrit_iast: adhvaryubahvṛcaiḥ samayaṃ kṛtvā dīkṣerannevamavilopo bhavatīti bhavatīti
meaning: अध्वर्युबह्वृचैः समयं कृत्वा दीक्षेरन्नेवमविलोपो भवतीति भवतीति
text_mt: "Having made an agreement with the adhvaryus and the Ṛgvedic priests, they should consecrate themselves; thus there is no disruption," [says the tradition].

title: atha navamī kaṇḍikā
text_mt: Everywhere, the brahman priest should sit to the south facing north, except for the oblations.
They call the sacrifices in a single domestic fire pākayajñas.
When they are about to offer oblations in these, he should sit silently; when the oblation is offered, he may do as he pleases.

sanskrit_iast: śūlagave ca balīn hṛyamāṇānanugacchennidhīyamānānāṃ dakṣiṇataḥ sthitvā nihiteṣvapa upaspṛśyānapekṣaṃ pratyāvrajet
meaning: शूलगवे च बलीन् हृयमाणाननुगच्छेन्निधीयमानानां दक्षिणतः स्थित्वा निहितेष्वप उपस्पृश्यानपेक्षं प्रत्याव्रजेत्
text_mt: And at the Śūlagava sacrifice, he should follow the offerings as they are being carried away, stand to the south of them as they are being laid down, and once they are laid down, having touched water, he should return without looking back.
In a pākayajña, he should accept the priestly fee silently, or with "Om".
The priestly fee for an animal sacrifice is an animal itself; a full vessel [is the fee] for a sthālīpāka.
Or for both, according to ability.
At the beginning of all ritual acts, he should await the direction of the adhvaryu.
And when no door is specified, he should enter through the eastern door.

sanskrit_iast: agnyādheye dakṣiṇayā dvārā prapadya cātuṣpraśyaṃ nirvapsyatsu tūṣṇīmupaviśet
meaning: अग्न्याधेये दक्षिणया द्वारा प्रपद्य चातुष्प्रश्यं निर्वप्स्यत्सु तूष्णीमुपविशेत्
text_mt: At the establishment of the sacred fires, having entered by the southern door, when they are about to measure out the rice for the four priests, he should sit down silently.
In the very same way, when they are about to take it up [from the fire].
If they make the officiating priests eat that, having taken the grains, they should discard them, saying, "Not in the sacrifice are they made discarded."
Then they should put in others, after the [twigs of the] aśvattha tree have been offered.
When the two fire-drills for the fire that is to be established have been handed over, he may do as he pleases.

sanskrit_iast: pūrvāhṇe dakṣiṇenāgnyāyatanāni gatvā yatrāgniṃ manthiṣyantaḥ syustaddakṣiṇato nirastaḥ parāvasuriti dakṣiṇā tṛṇaṃ nirasyedāvasoḥ sadane sīdāmītyupaviśet bhūrbhuvaḥsvarbṛhaspatirbrahmāhaṃ mānuṣaomityetenopaviśet yajuṣeti yatra syāt
meaning: पूर्वाह्णे दक्षिणेनाग्न्यायतनानि गत्वा यत्राग्निं मन्थिष्यन्तः स्युस्तद्दक्षिणतो निरस्तः परावसुरिति दक्षिणा तृणं निरस्येदावसोः सदने सीदामीत्युपविशेत् भूर्भुवःस्वर्बृहस्पतिर्ब्रह्माहं मानुषओमित्येतेनोपविशेत् यजुषेति यत्र स्यात्
text_mt: In the forenoon, having gone to the south of the hearths of the sacred fires, where they are about to churn the fire, [he should sit] to the south of that; he should cast away a blade of grass to the south with the formula, "Parāvasu is cast away"; he should sit down with, "I sit in the seat of Āvasu"; where it is prescribed, "With this yajus-formula he should sit down," he should sit down with, "Bhūḥ, bhuvaḥ, svaḥ; Bṛhaspati is the brahman priest; I am the human one; Om."
He should follow the fire as it is being brought forward, just as it goes.
Standing to the south of it as it is being laid down, when it has been laid down, he should sit down with a yajus-formula.
"Here [he should use] the first [formula]," says Śāṇḍilya.
"The second [formula]," says Dhānañjayya.

sanskrit_iast: jāte rathantaraṃ gāyedvāmadevy hriyamāṇe bṛhannihite sarvāṇi tṛceṣu manasā
meaning: जाते रथन्तरं गायेद्वामदेव्य् ह्रियमाणे बृहन्निहिते सर्वाणि तृचेषु मनसा
text_mt: When [the fire] is produced, he should sing the Rathantara melody; the Vāmadevya melody while it is being carried forward; the Bṛhat melody when it has been laid down; all of them mentally on triplets.
"In place of the first and the last, the Vāravantīya and Yajñāyajñīya melodies [should be sung]," says Lāmakāyana.
"In the former procedure, there is greater abundance," says Dhānañjayya.

title: atha daśamī kaṇḍikā
text_mt: When they are about to churn, having touched the two fire-drills, he should sing on the two fire-drills.
While [the fire] is being churned, [he should sing] either of the two [sāmans] on "agniṃ naraḥ".
When it blazes up, on "adarśi gātuḥ".
Or whatever [sāmans] the adhvaryu specifies to him, those he should sing.
Some say these are the duty of the udgātṛ priest, because of the Vedic text: "The udgātṛ priest [acts] by means of the Sāmaveda."
Just as the Vihavya, Sajanīya, and Kayāśubhīya hymns belong to the hotṛ priest;
and the preludes of the Vairāja and Śakkarī melodies belong to the prastotṛ priest;
and because [the singing] is not prescribed for all those who perform the office of the brahman priest;
and because of the connection with the ritual action of the udgātṛ priest, [for it is said:] "The four principal priests partake of it," that is, the partaking of the food for the four priests.
However, [the singing belongs] to the brahman priest, on account of the general governing rule;
and the singing of sāmans by this [brahman priest] is seen in the Vājapeya and Sautrāmaṇī sacrifices.
The mention of "udgātṛ priest" is because he is the principal [singer].
The Vihavya and other hymns [belong to the hotṛ priest] because of the prescription in the duties of the hotṛ priest.

sanskrit_iast: virāṭsu sruvanti purīṣeṇa sruvata iti bahuśruteḥ
meaning: विराट्सु स्रुवन्ति पुरीषेण स्रुवत इति बहुश्रुतेः
text_mt: Because of many Vedic passages, such as: "They sruva-offer upon the Virāj verses; they sruva-offer with the loose earth."
The absence of prescription is due to conflict of rules.
The connection with the ritual action is only as far as the text states.
When the full offering has been offered, he may do as he pleases.
If they offer oblation upon dice, having gone there, he should sit down silently.
While they gamble with them, he may do as he pleases.
In all rites beginning with the iṣṭis, he should sit down with a yajus formula,
The passage between him and the āhavanīya fire is for the patron of the sacrifice, not for others.

sanskrit_iast: taṃ yadādhvaryyurbrūyād brahmannidaṃ kariṣyāmīti savitṛprasūto'daḥ kuru bhūrbhuvaḥsvarbṛhaspatirbrahmāhaṃ mānuṣa omityetenānumantrayeta
meaning: तं यदाध्वर्य्युर्ब्रूयाद् ब्रह्मन्निदं करिष्यामीति सवितृप्रसूतोऽदः कुरु भूर्भुवःस्वर्बृहस्पतिर्ब्रह्माहं मानुष ओमित्येतेनानुमन्त्रयेत
text_mt: When the adhvaryu priest says to him, 'O Brahman, I shall do this,' he should give assent with this [formula]: 'Impelled by Savitṛ, do that! Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ, Svaḥ! Bṛhaspati is the Brahman, I am a mortal. Om!'

title: atha ekādaśī kaṇḍikā
text_mt: While the praṇītā waters are being brought forward, he should restrain his speech until they are released.
Or [he should restrain speech] while they are being brought forward until the call to the preparer of oblation, or from the stambayajus formula until the kindling-stick of departure.

sanskrit_iast: yatra vādhvaryyubṛhvṛcau ceṣṭetāṃ yatra vā na ceṣṭetāṃ vāgayataḥ prāyastveva syāt
meaning: यत्र वाध्वर्य्युबृह्वृचौ चेष्टेतां यत्र वा न चेष्टेतां वागयतः प्रायस्त्वेव स्यात्
text_mt: Where the adhvaryu priest and the ṛgvedic priest [the hotṛ] are active, or where they are not active, he should generally remain restrained in speech.

sanskrit_iast: prāyaścittañcetkarttavysyād bhūḥ svāheti gārhapatye juhuyāt bhuvaḥ svāheti dakṣiṇāgnāvāgnīdhrīye sutyācet svaḥ svāhetyāhavanīye bhūrbhuvaḥsvaḥ svāheti tatraiva
meaning: प्रायश्चित्तञ्चेत्कर्त्तव्य्स्याद् भूः स्वाहेति गार्हपत्ये जुहुयात् भुवः स्वाहेति दक्षिणाग्नावाग्नीध्रीये सुत्याचेत् स्वः स्वाहेत्याहवनीये भूर्भुवःस्वः स्वाहेति तत्रैव
text_mt: If an expiation is to be performed, he should offer into the gārhapatya fire with 'Bhūḥ svāhā', into the dakṣiṇa fire with 'Bhuvaḥ svāhā'—or into the āgnīdhra fire if it is a soma-pressing day—into the āhavanīya fire with 'Svaḥ svāhā', and into that very fire with 'Bhūrbhuvaḥsvaḥ svāhā'.
Having offered, he should say, 'Proceed, we have made the expiation.'

sanskrit_iast: avelāyāṃ cedvyāharedayajñiyaṃ vāpadyetaitā eva vyāhṛtīranuprekṣetedaṃ viṣṇuriti varcam
meaning: अवेलायां चेद्व्याहरेदयज्ञियं वापद्येतैता एव व्याहृतीरनुप्रेक्षेतेदं विष्णुरिति वर्चम्
text_mt: If he speaks out of turn or utters what is unfit for sacrifice, he should contemplate those very mystic utterances [vyāhṛtis], or the verse 'Idaṃ viṣṇur [vicakrame]...'.
On the new moon day, they should cleanse the milking-strainers with the [verses] beginning with 'Āpo hi ṣṭhā'.
'In all iṣṭis,' says Śāṇḍilyāyana.

sanskrit_iast: prāśitramāhriyamāṇaṃ pratimantrayeta mitrasya tvā cakṣuṣā pratipaśyāmīti
meaning: प्राशित्रमाह्रियमाणं प्रतिमन्त्रयेत मित्रस्य त्वा चक्षुषा प्रतिपश्यामीति
text_mt: When the prāśitra portion is being brought, he should address it with: 'With the eye of Mitra I look upon you.'
Having sipped water, he should receive it with: 'At the impulse of the divine [Savitṛ]...'

sanskrit_iast: vyūhya tṛṇāni purastāddaṇḍe sādayet pṛthivyāstvā nābhau sādayāmīti
meaning: व्यूह्य तृणानि पुरस्ताद्दण्डे सादयेत् पृथिव्यास्त्वा नाभौ सादयामीति

text_mt: Taking it with his thumb and ring-finger, he should eat it with: 'I eat you with the mouth of Agni,' and swallow it without chewing.

sanskrit_iast: apa ācamyorasi pāṇiṃ nidadhītendrasya tvā jaṭhare sādayāmīti
meaning: अप आचम्योरसि पाणिं निदधीतेन्द्रस्य त्वा जठरे सादयामीति
text_mt: Having sipped water, he should place his hand on his chest with: 'I settle you in the belly of Indra.'
Having washed the prāśitra vessel, he should set it down there.
Or he should have it carried back just as it was brought.
When the brahman's portion is brought, he should place it near there.
He should eat it when the iṣṭi is concluded.
When the anvāhārya mess of boiled rice is brought, he should touch it silently,
or with: 'You are the share of Prajāpati.'

sanskrit_iast: athāparaṃ prajāpaterbhāgo'syūrjasvānyayasvānakṣito'syakṣityai tvā prāṇāpānau me pāhi samānavyānau me pāhyudānarūpe me pāhyūrgasyūrjaṃ mayi dhehīti
meaning: अथापरं प्रजापतेर्भागोऽस्यूर्जस्वान्ययस्वानक्षितोऽस्यक्षित्यै त्वा प्राणापानौ मे पाहि समानव्यानौ मे पाह्युदानरूपे मे पाह्यूर्गस्यूर्जं मयि धेहीति
text_mt: Now the other [formula]: 'You are the share of Prajāpati, vigorous, rich in milk, imperishable; for imperishability [I touch] you. Protect my expiration and inspiration; protect my equal breath and diffused breath; protect my upward breath and form; you are vigor, bestow vigor in me!'

sanskrit_iast: tatraiva yajamānaṃ vācayet prajāpatiṃ tvayā samakṣādadhyāsamāgamyā anvāhāryyaṃ dadāni brahman brahmāsi brahmaṇe tvā hutādya mā mā hsiīrahuto mahyśivo bhaveti
meaning: तत्रैव यजमानं वाचयेत् प्रजापतिं त्वया समक्षादध्यासमागम्या अन्वाहार्य्यं ददानि ब्रह्मन् ब्रह्मासि ब्रह्मणे त्वा हुताद्य मा मा ह्सिईरहुतो मह्य्शिवो भवेति

sanskrit_iast: samidhaṃ prasthānīyāmanumantrayeta deva savitaretatte yajñaṃ prāhurbṛhaspataye brahmaṇe tena yajñamava tena yajñapatiṃ tena māmava mano jūtirjuṣatāmājyasya bṛhaspatiryajñamimaṃ tanotvariṣṭaṃ yajñsamimaṃ dadhātu viśve devāsa iha mādayantāmityupāśu pratiṣṭhetyuccaiḥ
meaning: समिधं प्रस्थानीयामनुमन्त्रयेत देव सवितरेतत्ते यज्ञं प्राहुर्बृहस्पतये ब्रह्मणे तेन यज्ञमव तेन यज्ञपतिं तेन मामव मनो जूतिर्जुषतामाज्यस्य बृहस्पतिर्यज्ञमिमं तनोत्वरिष्टं यज्ञ्समिमं दधातु विश्वे देवास इह मादयन्तामित्युपाशु प्रतिष्ठेत्युच्चैः
title: atha dvādaśī kaṇḍikā
text_mt: He should follow the kindling-stick of departure with the formula: 'O divine Savitṛ, this sacrifice they have proclaimed to you, to Bṛhaspati the Brahman; thereby protect the sacrifice, thereby the lord of sacrifice, thereby protect me! May the impulse of the mind enjoy the ghee! May Bṛhaspati extend this sacrifice, may he preserve this uninjured sacrifice! May all the gods rejoice here!'—in a low voice; and 'Pratiṣṭhā' aloud.
